references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: South Broad Street complete tower and south entrance: pale stone base and ornate projecting entrance, dark mansards and dormers, separate tall clock tower with columned gallery, pale tapering crown and dark Penn statue. Neighbors and street traffic are excluded.

references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: South facade upper detail: paired round columns, pediments, a projecting three-bay entrance pavilion, dark curved/sloping mansard panels, dormers and pale sculpture silhouettes. Fine ornament inventories are original approximations.

references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: South entry close: a physically open large round-headed passage, pale voussoirs, rusticated ground stone, paired columns and multiple cornice levels. Gates/advertising/traffic fixtures are excluded.

references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: Clock and crown: pale square clock stage with four large dark circular dials, corner columns and curved pediments; tall tapering white ribbed roof, dark sculpture silhouettes, upper circular viewing railing/pedestal and dark broad-brimmed Penn figure.

references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: Tower lower gallery and clock: long straight square stone shaft below an open outer colonnade around recessed tall arched glazing, strong projecting cornices and a separate clock cube. Preserve the separation of these stages.

references.credit: Elevated Angles for Visit Philadelphia; local observation only.
references.observed: Elevated south view shows complete square ensemble: four projecting corner roof pavilions, taller south portal mansard, long lower slate roofs/dormers, rear courtyard wings and separate north clock tower. Independent neighboring towers are excluded.

references.credit: Elevated Angles for Visit Philadelphia; local observation only.
references.observed: High Penn/crown view: original figure has broad hat, coat, separated legs and one extended hand; circular railed observation deck and ribbed pale tapered pedestal sit below it. The figure will be an original polygonal likeness, not a downloaded scan or claim of exact sculptural reproduction.

references.credit: Beyond My Ken,CC BY-SA4.0; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: Northwest courtyard: large open court, simpler pale inner walls, dark mansard strips/dormers, round projecting bay and ground entrances. Fine window/air-conditioning inventories are approximate; landscape and temporary fittings are excluded.

references.credit: Beyond My Ken,CC BY-SA4.0; local observation only, not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: South courtyard portal: two round staircase turrets with conical dark roofs flank a central upper arched window and an open low pedestrian passage. Keep the courtyard and passage physically open.

references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008;local reference only,not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: West facade complete: long pale two-principal-floor base, dormer row, dark mansard strips, raised entrance and corner pavilions, lower inner roofs and separate north clock tower. Full ensemble must remain present in all tiers.

references.credit: Mary Ann Sullivan2008;local reference only,not redistributed or used as a texture.
references.observed: Northwest distant overall: north portal, broad low ensemble, stepped tower shaft/colonnade/clock/tapering crown and Penn. Clock tower is on the north wing rather than the center of the courtyard.

method: Eleven ordinary photographs actually inspected, plus retained map and standard viewer PMTiles/global terrain. No bespoke survey, PDF, archival research, imported mesh or photograph texture. Photographs remain local reference only.
